source_refs.quoted_text: The test treats wells, not individual water samples, as replicates. Pooling all 108 sample-level records into a sample-by-sample comparison would count every well 6 times and would overstate the evidence; the reported p-value rests on the 18 well-level scores alone. Because the sign test uses only the direction of each well's change, it is insensitive to the size of individual shifts and to the spread of baseline concentrations across wells (4.20-13.70 mg/L).

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to show that the reported p-value could only have come from entering wells repeatedly into a row-independent test. I recomputed the exact two-sided binomial sign test on the 18 well-level signs derived independently from the raw rows: 15 of 18 wells declined, giving p = 2 x (C(18,15)+C(18,16)+C(18,17)+C(18,18))/2^18 = 1976/262144 = 0.007538, which matches the reported p exactly. A row-level version of the analysis would have used n = 108 samples or n = 54 round-level pairs, which cannot reproduce p = 0.007538 with 15/18 declines. I also traced the code path: binomtest receives n_down and n_tested computed from the per-well change scores produced by collapse_to_wells, with no branch that passes sample-level rows into the test, and spot-checked three wells' means and signs against the CSV (all consistent). The falsification failed on every check, so the issue class is not demonstrated.
